purpose: Records the 2026-09-30 fix of the required osv-scanner check, which fails on fresh runs since four advisories were published that day (14:46Z to 15:00Z): GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw and GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g (urllib3 2.7.0, all fixed in 2.8.0) in the OpenHands recipe lock, and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (next 16.3.5, fixed in 16.3.6) in the frozen macOS variant lock. The OpenHands lock is relocked onto urllib3 2.8.0 with the recipe's own method (only urllib3's version and hashes change); the macOS lock is a frozen evidence artifact with no live owner and gets an ignore under the repository's policy, an IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS row and a pnpm reader that bounds the repo-wide ignore. One change carries both, because the check scans the whole inventory.
authorization: Requested by session sota-default-harness-setup (c5), whose PR #540 was blocked, in a cross-session message on 2026-09-30, which asked the OpenHands lock lane (issue #518, owner bc) to take the urllib3 relock and to name the owner of the macOS lock. The macOS lock has no live owner: its only commit is #201 (2026-09-24) and no session claims it. No user decision is needed: both fixes follow the repository's own policy and method.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's command line, a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv, and reads of git objects and the OSV API. Static and local; not an execution of the recipe, of any worker or of any application.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock (pins.json source_archive), which still pins urllib3 2.7.0 or older, and the grader venv has its own lock; neither is changed here (the same scope limit as the PyJWT relock record).

The macOS ignore is a reachability statement about this repository only: the repository keeps the variant's package.json and lock (two files, no application source), so it says nothing about the application that ran on the Mac in 2026-09-24. It expires on 2026-12-24 and then needs a renewed dated reason, or the lock leaving the inventory.

The Python guard (python_pins) reads no npm format. The repo-wide next ignore is therefore bounded by the new pnpm_next_pins reader and its test, which read pnpm lockfileVersion 9 keys strictly and fail closed; a future non-pnpm npm lock (package-lock.json, yarn.lock) pinning an affected next would not be seen by it.
Section E of the returned outputs is a local run of the workflow's command, not the CI run; the required check on this change is the CI result.

Codex's draft PR #535 replaces this lock with a Linux-only lock (sha256 383ccc5b87702174e471732872f002f1621186710402d048acc2b1910306e106) that carries urllib3 2.7.0 too, so it needs the same bump and a new digest in its exact-lock entry before it can pass the check; this change does not touch #535's files.
